newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Apple and Pear board says Frucor juice for sale.
newsitem.headline: NZ Apple and Pear board says Frucor juice for sale.

text.p: The Apple and Pear Board has offered Auckland fruit juice company Frucor Beverages for sale, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
Directors of the board and of Frucor Holdings said in a statement a sale would go ahead if "premium value" could be obtained for the company.
Frucor is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Frucor Holdings, owned by the Apple and Pear Marketing Board, which also trades as ENZA.
Frucor chairman and ENZA chief executive Gary Smith said the decision followed a strategic review of core businesses.

The board, although reluctant to sell what had been a very successful business for many years, believed Frucor would benefit from ownership that could provide the capital resources needed for future growth and development.
Although the NZAPMB no longer controls market sales or the processing sector it has a concentrate processing unit that typically turns 150,000 tonnes of apples into concentrate a year.
Frucor's brands include Fresh Up, Just Juice, McCoys and Citrus Tree.
Smith said the company had a strong position in New Zealand and had prospects in an expanding export market in Asia and the Pacific.
The appointment of an advisor to handle the sale project is expected to be announced shortly.
Market sources said a float was one option that might be considered by Frucor.
